title: The Origin of Gods: Why Early Humans Created Religion
description:
How did the concept of God sneak into the human brain? And when did Homo sapiens first imagine unseen forces controlling their lives? This video from Pale Blue Thoughts traces the origin of gods and religion through human evolution.

From the days when our frail ancestors huddled in caves, terrified of thunder and lightning, to the invention of agriculture, writing, and cooperation, humans sought explanations for the unknown. Stories like the Epic of Gilgamesh and Enuma Elish reveal how imagination filled gaps in knowledge. As writing evolved from Sumerian cuneiform to Egyptian hieroglyphs, myths became more elaborate — just like J.K. Rowling weaving magic into Harry Potter.

We also explore the biology of belief: how language evolved with the help of the FOXP2 “language gene”, Broca’s area, Wernicke’s area, and the supra-laryngeal vocal tract. Once humans could communicate, they began to invent fictional realities — gods, curses, afterlives, and devils. Dreams of dead relatives begging for food gave rise to the afterlife concept, while the spread of infectious diseases birthed ghosts and demons.

Religion also served practical purposes: offerings to appease angry gods were taken by priests, the first “influencers,” who exploited fear and greed. Over time, grains became livestock, and finally even humans were sacrificed — a tradition that echoes in some practices today.

If you’ve searched for origins of religion, why humans believe in gods, evolution of gods, man created god, afterlife origins, agriculture and religion, language and belief, or Pale Blue Thoughts, this video breaks down how humans turned fear and imagination into faith.
